title: Shout one fixed value, or each value you are given

blocks.text: The same method, `String::toUpperCase`, can be a **bound** reference (the receiver is one object, fixed when the reference is made) or an **unbound** one (the receiver is whatever string the function is handed).
A `Holder` keeps one changeable string (`get()` and `set(String)`). Write three methods in `Shout`:

items: `Supplier<String> of(Holder holder)` returns a supplier that upper-cases the value the holder has **when `of` is called**. Use a bound reference.
`Function<String, String> each()` upper-cases whatever string it is given. Use an unbound reference.
`List<String> all(List<String> words)` upper-cases every word, in order.

blocks.text: If the holder's value is `null`, `of` throws a `NullPointerException` with the message `value must not be null` straight away. Think about when a bound reference reads its receiver, and what that means when the holder changes afterwards.

cases.says: It upper-cases the holder's value and each word it is given.
A bound reference captures its receiver when it is made, so a later change to the holder does not reach it.
A null receiver fails when the supplier is made, with the message 'value must not be null', not later when it is called.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A bound reference always calls its one captured object, while an unbound reference calls whatever object it is handed.
A bound reference evaluates its receiver when the reference is made, so a null receiver fails at once.
